en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa-kanda
2. The Training Rule on Expelling a Thief At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, in Vesālī, the wife of a certain Licchavi was unfaithful.
Then that Licchavi said this to the woman:
"Please desist; I will surely bring you harm.
Even when addressed in this way, she did not heed him.
Now at that time, the Licchavi assembly was gathered in Vesālī for some business or other.
Then that Licchavi said this to those Licchavis:
“Noble sirs, please grant me one woman.”
“Who is she? “My wife is being unfaithful; I shall have her killed.
“Find out.”
That woman heard:
"My husband, they say, wishes to have me killed.
Taking her most precious belongings, she went to Sāvatthī, approached the non-Buddhist sectarians, and requested ordination.
The members of other sects did not wish to grant him the going-forth.
He approached the bhikkhunīs and requested the going-forth;
yet the bhikkhunīs also did not wish to grant him the going-forth.
Having approached the bhikkhunī Thullanandā and shown her his belongings, he requested the going forth.
The bhikkhunī Thullanandā took his belongings and gave him the going forth.
Then that Licchavi, searching for that woman, went to Sāvatthī; having seen her gone forth among the bhikkhunīs, he approached King Pasenadi of Kosala.
Having approached King Pasenadi of Kosala, he said this to him:
“Your Majesty, my wife has arrived at Sāvatthī taking the excellent gift;
may Your Majesty grant her permission.”
“In that case, my good man, search for her and report back.
“She has been seen, Your Majesty; she has gone forth among the bhikkhunīs.
“If, my good man, she has gone forth among the bhikkhunīs, nothing can be done to her.”
“The Dhamma has been well-proclaimed by the Blessed One; let one lead the holy life for the complete ending of suffering.
Then that Licchavi complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying, “How can these bhikkhunīs give the going-forth to a thief?”
The bhikkhunīs heard that Licchavi criticizing, disparaging, and complaining.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as before]... criticized, disparaged, and complained, saying:
"How can the noble lady Thullanandā give the going-forth to a thief?"
Then those bhikkhunīs reported this matter to the bhikkhus... [as before] ...
"Is it true, bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā ordains a female thief?
"It is true, Blessed One."
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How indeed, bhikkhus, can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā give the going-forth to a thief?
This, bhikkhus, is neither for the pleasing of those without confidence nor for the increase of those with confidence…” [and so on].
And furthermore, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule as follows: “Whatever nun,
knowing that a female thief has been identified as deserving the death penalty, should ordain her— without having obtained permission from the king,
the Saṅgha, a group, a guild, or a clan, except in a case of legal exemption— this nun also incurs an offense of immediate transgression.”
"Having committed an offense that is a *saṅghādisesa*, which is a formal meeting of the Saṅgha and entails sending away.
*Yā pana* means "whichever [nun]"; such as... [and so forth].
"Bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Knows" means:
She either knows it herself, or others inform her of it, or she informs [the owner] herself.
One called a "thief" (corī) is one who takes what has not been given, which is reckoned as theft, having a value of five māsakas or more than five māsakas; such a person is called a thief.
"One deserving of death" means that having committed [an offense], she has reached the state of being deserving of death.
"Known" means...
She is known by other people as "she is to be executed.
Without having obtained leave means without having asked for permission.
"A king" means wherever a king rules, that king is to be consulted.
"The Sangha" means...
The community of bhikkhunīs is what is meant; the community of bhikkhunīs must be informed.
A group is that where a group instructs; the group must be informed.
A "guild" (pūga) is where a guild governs; the guild must be informed. A "clan" (seṇi) is...
[as above].
Wherever a guild governs, the guild must be consulted;
except for what is permissible,
meaning excluding that which is allowable.
“Kappa” means two kinds of kappa: she has gone forth among the sectarians, or she has gone forth among other bhikkhunīs.

If, except when it is a kappa, she seeks out a group, a preceptor, a bowl, or a robe with the intention, “I will give the full admission,” or if she demarcates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
For the motion, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
For two proclamations, there are offenses of serious transgression (thullaccaya).
At the conclusion of the proclamation, the preceptor incurs an offense entailing suspension (saṅghādisesa).
There is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa) for the group and for the preceptor.
The phrase "this too" is said with reference to what preceded it.
"An offense of the first category" means that one commits it simultaneously with the transgression of the matter itself, without having been formally admonished.
"Leading to expulsion" means...
He is expelled from the Saṅgha. Because it involves formal meeting with the Saṅgha (saṅghena ādisetabbaṃ),
it is therefore called a *saṅghādisesa*.
If she ordains one who is a thief, perceiving her as a thief, except when it is allowable, there is an offense entailing suspension (saṅghādisesa).
If she ordains one who is a thief, being doubtful about it, except when it is allowable, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If she ordains one who is a thief, perceiving her as not a thief, except when it is allowable, there is no offense.
If it is not a thief, but one perceives it as a thief, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If it is not a thief, but one is doubtful, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is not a thief, and one perceives it as not a thief, there is no offense.
There is no offense if she ordains one without knowing [the facts],
or if she ordains one after having obtained permission.
One ordains one who has made a formal agreement; [the offense is not incurred] in the case of one who is insane,
or for one who is a first-time offender.
The second Saṅghādisesa training rule is concluded.
